title: One bit flipped. Which one?
hook: A parity check can tell you a message got damaged. Can three checks tell you where?

knows: a parity check notices an odd number of flipped bits (two-flips-slip-by)
doesNotKnow: that several overlapping parity checks can locate, and so correct, a single flipped bit

misconception: Error detection can say something is wrong but cannot say where.
objective: The learner can read the failing checks of a 7-bit Hamming word (checks 2 and 3 fail, worth 2 + 4) as the position of the flipped bit (6), and say that flipping it back repairs the word.

claims.text: The sent word 0110011 passes all three checks over positions {1,3,5,7}, {2,3,6,7} and {4,5,6,7}: each holds an even number of 1s.
claims.source: Demo.tsx fails(received(null)) = [false, false, false]. Builder ran the same parity sums in Node: [0,0,0]. 0110011 is the Hamming(7,4) codeword for data 1011 at positions 3,5,6,7.

claims.text: Flipping bit 6 makes checks 2 and 3 fail and check 1 pass; their worths 2 + 4 add up to 6.
claims.source: Node: flipping position 6 of 0110011 gives 0110001; parities [0,1,1]; 2 + 4 = 6. Demo.tsx TARGET_FAILS, TARGET_SUM.

claims.text: For every single flipped bit, the worths of the failing checks add up to that bit's position, and each position fails a different set of checks.
claims.source: Node, all 7 positions: sums 1,2,3,4,5,6,7, all distinct. Follows from position p lying in check k exactly when bit k of p (in binary) is 1 (Hamming 1950).

claims.text: A check fails when its bits hold an odd number of 1s.
claims.source: Even-parity convention used by the stage (Hamming 1950; any coding-theory text, e.g. MacKay, Information Theory, Inference and Learning Algorithms, 1.2).

claims.text: Flipping the located bit back repairs the word, not just flags it.
claims.source: Flipping a bit twice restores it; with one error the located position is the flipped one (c3). Only single-bit errors are claimed.

claims.text: Richard Hamming published this code in 1950.
claims.source: R. W. Hamming, 'Error detecting and error correcting codes', Bell System Technical Journal 29(2), 147-160, April 1950.

recall.question: With the same three checks (worth 1, 2 and 4), one bit flipped and only checks 1 and 3 fail. Which bit do you flip back?
recall.why: The failing checks are worth 1 and 4, and 1 + 4 = 5: bit 5 is the only position in checks 1 and 3 but not check 2.
